**No `ingest: partial` marker anywhere in `wiki/`** and **no stubs** (`*Stub — to be expanded.*` appears only in `log.md` history) — the previous pass finished what it started, so this pass began new files rather than resuming one.

**Backlog audit.** Matching `raw/` filenames against each source page's first 4,000 characters (title + `**Article:**` line + bibliographic block) — slugs are abbreviated and score near zero, so filename-to-slug matching is useless. **617 `raw/` files; ~35 uningested tier-1 guideline/consensus documents remain**, concentrated in `raw/GI Guidelines/Other/` and `/EASL/` and named in Nick's own `Society Year Topic (FirstAuthor)` style — his drops, which take priority. Lectures and chalk talks score low on the same audit and are **not** candidates (gating: never auto-ingest). **Backlog mode stays ON.**

**Ingest target picked:** `raw/GI Guidelines/ASGE/ASGE 2025 Endoscopic Diagnosis and Management of Adult IBD Consensus (Shen).pdf` — US society, 2025, and it supersedes parts of two 2015 ASGE documents the wiki still leans on ([[asge-2015-ibd]], [[asge-2015-scenic-ibd-dysplasia]]).

**Sources created:**

- `[[asge-2025-ibd-endoscopy-consensus]]` — *Endoscopic diagnosis and management of adult inflammatory bowel disease: a consensus document from the ASGE IBD Endoscopy Consensus Panel* (Shen et al., *Gastrointest Endosc* 2025;101:295–314). **All 38 consensus statements captured with the document's own agreement percentages, and all 17 statements that failed consensus**, which the panel publishes separately (Table 2). **Methodology recorded prominently: modified Delphi — no systematic review, no GRADE, no recommendation strength anywhere.** The only quantitative attribute a statement carries is the share of panelists voting agree/strongly agree (consensus = >80%, excluding neutral and no-expertise votes, which were not counted in the denominator). Statement numbering is the document's own.

**Pages updated (ASGE 2025 IBD ingest):**

- `[[inflammatory-bowel-disease]]` — new `## Index Endoscopy and Biopsy Protocol`, the cross-cutting rules that belong to neither disease script alone: indication (chronic diarrhea >4–6 wk, persistent bleeding, new or unexplained anemia, weight loss, growth failure), the **≥4 biopsy sets** (terminal ileum, right colon, left colon, rectum) **plus every reachable stricture**, **biopsy before starting medical therapy** (treated UC turns patchy in ~⅓ of patients), the **3-samples-per-region minimum**, and where to aim (strictures, nodular and inflamed mucosa, **ulcer edge**). Two callouts: the three histologic findings that settle an ambiguous biopsy (Paneth cell metaplasia 0%–1.9% in non-IBD distal colon; pyloric gland metaplasia; granulomas in only 9%–67% of CD) and the two mimics diagnosed by *where* you biopsy (SCAD spares the rectum → biopsy the rectum; prolapse/solitary rectal ulcer → anterior wall). Router row added; both disease scripts link in rather than copy.
- `[[ulcerative-colitis]]` — **every colonic or rectal UC stricture biopsied at least yearly** (added to the existing "cancer until proven otherwise" pitfall); **diverted large bowel after >8–10 y of colitis → surveillance biopsy q1–3 y** (rectal-stump cancer 3.9–4.5 per 1000 diverted patient-years); the **CMV sampling protocol** (base *and* edge of ulcer, several colonic sites, 11 samples by flex sig in UC / 16 by colonoscopy in CD, >2 IHC-positive cells per sample independently associated with colectomy, tissue PCR without histology of unclear significance); surveil in endoscopic remission and describe lesions by site/size/Paris shape/surrounding inflammation; the targeted-vs-random split with the **Seattle protocol "being phased out" for average-risk patients** and why PSC/tubular colon/prior invisible dysplasia keep random biopsies (**nonconventional dysplasia — hypermucinous, goblet cell–deficient, crypt cell — is often endoscopically invisible**).
- `[[crohns-disease]]` — EGD indication widened (**all** pediatric suspected CD, not only symptomatic patients; Montreal L4); **biopsy every colonic, rectal and anorectal stricture at index then q1–3 y**; two new surgical-referral rows (**recurrence needing endotherapy more often than q3–6 mo**; fistula/abscess-associated or previously refractory); outcome definitions (reintervention-free and surgery-free survival, and the **absence** of any agreed short-term success definition); the postoperative clock **restarting at stoma closure** and the **q1–3 y** interval after the index 6–12 mo exam; **ileoscopy past the fascia before closing a temporary diversion**; large (>1 cm) inflammatory polyps removable, with post-inflammatory polyps as a neoplasia marker (OR 2.54).
- `[[pouchitis]]` — the **three-tier pouch surveillance table** (yearly for precolectomy colitis-associated neoplasia, 1–3 y for PSC/chronic pouchitis/CD of the pouch/chronic cuffitis/family history of CRC, 3 y average risk), the **five pouchoscopy landmarks** to report (prepouch ileum, **inlet**, pouch body, **anastomosis**, cuff), biopsy sites and what they uncover, and that **ulceration and ulcerated surface area in the pouch body** is the one consistently reproducible observation.
- `[[ibd-endoscopic-scoring]]` — **a decision gap the page had flagged for itself is now closed.** The SES-CD ulcer-size row was reproduced as published from [[aga-2024-ibd-endoscopic-scoring]], which prints only three of four levels (*"0 if absent, 1 if between 0.1–0.5 cm, 2 if larger than 2 cm"*), omits the 0.5–2 cm band and gives >2 cm **2 points instead of 3**. ASGE 2025 Figure 1 prints **all four bands with an endoscopic image of each** — 0 none, 1 aphthous 0.1–0.5 cm, 2 large 0.5–2 cm, 3 very large >2 cm — so the table is now complete and the AGA wording is identified as a misprint rather than left as an unexplained hole. Also added: **ulceration is the line between MES 2 and 3** (MES 2 = granularity, no ulceration).
- `[[primary-sclerosing-cholangitis]]` — the ASGE 2025 colonic rule, which is **stricter than AASLD 2022 on both counts**: **yearly** (not 1–2 y) surveillance colonoscopy in PSC with UC or large-bowel CD, **regardless of extent and duration**, with **NBI or chromoendoscopy mandatory** (not optional as in average-risk IBD) **and both targeted and random biopsies**.
- `[[capsule-endoscopy]]` — the pooled CD retention rates (overall **3.32%**, suspected **2.35%**, established **4.63%**, adult 3.49% vs pediatric 1.64%) and the full gating rule (passed patency capsule, no obstructive symptoms, inconclusive ileocolonoscopy and/or small-bowel imaging); plus the note that **push/device-assisted enteroscopy in that same situation failed consensus**.
- `[[intestinal-ultrasound]]` — *Limitations* now records that **adoption is ahead of the consensus**: IUS "can be considered, where available", while the statement *encouraging* onsite IUS **failed to reach consensus**, with equipment and training named as the barriers.
- `[[ostomy-management]]` — two pointers (ileoscopy past the fascia before closure; diverted-bowel surveillance), each to the page that owns the decision.

**Contradictions surfaced (4, all genuine, none silently resolved):**

- **ASGE softened its own SCENIC consensus.** [[asge-2015-scenic-ibd-dysplasia]] recommends chromoendoscopy **over** white light. ASGE 2025 passed the statement making **HD white light *or* image-enhanced endoscopy** acceptable (statement 28) and **failed** the statement that would have *recommended* image enhancement (Table 2 #12). Enhanced imaging stays mandatory only in the PSC group. Recorded on [[ulcerative-colitis]] with the head-to-head meta-analyses (HD NBI > chromoendoscopy > white light on network meta-analysis; **no difference between dye-based and virtual** chromoendoscopy on any dysplasia endpoint).
- **Pouch surveillance moves PSC out of the annual tier.** ASGE 2015 and AGA 2021 both put PSC alongside prior colorectal dysplasia/cancer at annual pouchoscopy; ASGE 2025 keeps only **precolectomy neoplasia** annual and drops PSC, chronic pouchitis, CD of the pouch and chronic cuffitis to 1–3 y. Newest same-tier document → it governs [[pouchitis]], flagged on the page. **Colonic** surveillance in PSC-IBD is unaffected and in fact tightened to annual.
- **Stents in benign IBD strictures: ASGE against, AGA permits.** ASGE 2025 statement 34 says endoscopic stents **should not be used** for benign disease-associated or anastomotic strictures in pre- or postoperative CD or UC (an RCT of self-expandable metal stents failed to beat endoscopic balloon dilation). [[aga-2026-therapeutic-endoscopy-ibd]] keeps a fully covered stent as an option after failed dilation. **AGA 2026 is newer and governs [[crohns-disease]]**; the disagreement is stated inline.
- **Surveillance interval 1–5 y vs ACG's 1–3 y** — the document surfaces this itself (ACG caps at 3 y; AGA, ECCO and BSG allow 5 y). ASGE 2025 adopts the wider band and makes it patient-specific, matching the [[asge-acg-2024-colonoscopy-quality-indicators]] Table 13 grid already on the page; noted as corroboration rather than a change.

**Cards: 16 notes written, 2 rewritten in place (ids kept).** Tier-1 society consensus, so cardable.

- New: `a31d20`–`a31d22` on [[inflammatory-bowel-disease]] (index biopsy sets + timing, 3-per-region minimum, Paneth cell metaplasia); `c500a0`–`c500a2` on [[ulcerative-colitis]] (yearly stricture biopsy, diverted-bowel interval, CMV ulcer sampling); `cd2590`–`cd2593` on [[crohns-disease]] (stricture biopsy interval, the q3–6 mo retreatment trigger for surgery, ileoscopy past the fascia, postoperative interval); `ba1014`–`ba1015` on [[pouchitis]] (cuff + anal transition zone, the five landmarks); `0b5020` on [[ibd-endoscopic-scoring]] (the complete SES-CD ulcer bands); `5c0030` on [[primary-sclerosing-cholangitis]] (annual interval, extent and duration irrelevant).
- **Rewritten because they tested superseded facts, ids preserved:** `ba1010` (was "annual pouchoscopy for prior dysplasia/cancer **or PSC**" → now the three-tier interval table, re-sourced to ASGE 2025) and `5c001a` (tested AASLD's 1–2 y interval alongside the age-15 start; the contested interval moved to the correctly-sourced `5c0030`, and `5c001a` now tests the start age alone, which is uncontested).
- All ≤3 clozes, `{at:}` anchors set and checked against the pages' headings. Deliberately **not** carded: the capsule retention rates (incidence data, and the actionable patency-capsule rule is already carded as `cd2510`); "histologic healing is not a target" (already `d7a007` on [[treat-to-target-ibd]]); "a colon stricture in UC is malignant until proven otherwise" (already `c50043` — the new card tests the *interval*, a different unit); the SCAD rectal-sparing biopsy rule (answer duplicates `d5b001`).
- **Deck not rebuilt — `node` is blocked in this sandbox.** Card files are written; the 05:00 card pass builds and will report any problem.

**Ingested 2 — `[[weo-2024-large-colorectal-lst-consensus]]`** (Djinbachian, Rex, Chiu et al., *Digestive Endoscopy* 2024;36:1253–1268; World Endoscopy Organization Delphi consensus, tier 1). Picked as a **focused** document after ingest 1, to finish a whole file inside the remaining run budget rather than start a long one and leave it `partial`.

- Source page created with **all 42 consensus statements across the five tables**, each with the document's **GRADE strength, quality of evidence and agreement percentage** — unusually for a Delphi document, this one rates every statement, so it must not be relayed as ungraded. Also recorded: the round-by-round attrition (51 presented → 25 passed round 1 → 46 core statements → 39 → 3 more in round 3) and the **two topics dropped outright at <50% agreement**, which are findings in their own right.
- `[[polypectomy]]` — the **en bloc vs piecemeal decision table by optical class and site** (the rectum handled separately throughout), a pearl on **JNET 2B's 50.9% positive predictive value** against 2A's 91%–98.3% and the optional Kudo restratification, the **piece-count recurrence gradient** (~10% at 3 pieces, 25% at 4; residual tissue in 19.5% of margins and 23.8% of bases; **cold snare capped ~8 mm per piece**), submucosal invasion rates by morphology and site (proximal granular homogeneous **0.7%**, rectal **1.2%**), the rectum-specific strategy that cured 100% of potentially curable superficially invasive cancers, the three **required documentation** items for any ≥20 mm LST, the competency statements, **specimen handling** (pin in the endoscopy room, 2–3 mm parallel sections, desmin / D2-40 / Elastica van Gieson, **R0 = no neoplasia at the margins**), the **curative-resection grid** after en bloc R0, and follow-up (**6 mo after piecemeal, 1–3 y after en bloc R0**).
- `[[colorectal-esd]]` — the page's ESD indication set was **ungraded narrative text from USMSTF 2020, and said so**. WEO 2024 supplies the same three indications as **Strong** recommendations (en bloc difficult with EMR; submucosal fibrosis; chronic inflammation such as UC), plus the reimbursement statement, the **EID / PAEM** option for a lower-rectal lesion with suspected deep invasion in a patient declining surgery, and the French randomized controlled trial showing fewer recurrences with ESD but lower T1 rates in the EMR arm.

**Six deliberate non-answers recorded, not papered over:** no numeric threshold for low / moderate / high submucosal invasion risk; **no endorsement of any single optical classification** (that statement failed at <50% agreement, which is why JNET, Kudo, Paris, WASP and the LST classification appear as co-equals and statement 3.5 asks only that *some* invasion-predicting system be recorded); **no competency case number** (also dropped); **no recommendation at all** for a serrated lesion with an overt dysplastic focus; deep (≥1000 μm) submucosal invasion with no adverse features left to shared decision making; and the explicit allowance that **piecemeal when en bloc is recommended beats sending a benign lesion to surgery**.

**Printing inconsistency preserved:** statement 1.5's agreement is **95% in Table 1 and 93% in the body text** (strongly agree 44% + agree 49%). Both recorded; the body's arithmetic is self-consistent.

**Cards: 4 new notes on `[[polypectomy]]`** — `a9e101` (piece-count recurrence gradient), `a9e102` (the ~8 mm cold snare piece ceiling), `a9e103` (2–3 mm parallel sectioning), `a9e104` (1–3 y after en bloc R0, and what that exam looks for). Deliberately **not** carded, because the deck already owns the fact: en bloc-vs-piecemeal selection by LST morphology (`2f80d6`), JNET 2B histology (`1c7d44`), the two reasons to favour en bloc in the rectum (`9f3a08`), specimen pinning (`4b1d7e`), the five histologic criteria (`3e91c7`), post-piecemeal 6-month follow-up (`a70f35`, `c58004`), ESD-over-piecemeal-EMR lesion findings (`ce2001`), and cancer in a piecemeal specimen (`7a3bc4`). **Ingested 1 — `[[acs-2018-crc-screening]]`** (Wolf et al, *CA Cancer J Clin* 2018;68:250–281; guideline, tier 1):

- Source page created with all **6 recommendations** in ACS's own two-level strength vocabulary (***strong* / *qualified***, explicitly not the usual strong/weak pair), the 6-test option menu with intervals, Table 3 test-selection considerations condensed, and the age-to-begin / age-to-stop evidence. The document numbers nothing — the numbering on the page is flagged as the wiki's.
- `[[colorectal-cancer-screening]]` — added the **ACS column** to *When to Start and Stop*; added the ACS test menu note (deliberately unranked, mt-sDNA interval attributed to the **manufacturer**, low-sensitivity gFOBT not recommended, no capsule/blood test); added the **positive-FIT delay** cohort table (no excess risk ≤9 mo; **+48% CRC risk and double the stage III/IV risk at ≥10 mo**; OR 2.25 / 3.22 at ≥12 mo).
- **Contradiction surfaced and resolved:** ACS's ≥10-month inflection reads as conflicting with the **>6-month** threshold already on the page from [[aga-2022-noninvasive-crc-screening]]. AGA 2022 is newer, same tier → **AGA governs the page**; the ACS table is framed as where measurable harm begins, not as licence to wait. Noted on both the entity page and the source page's *Contradictions*.
- `[[early-onset-colorectal-cancer]]` — net-new, non-conflicting: the **birth-cohort effect quantified** (born ~1990 = 2× colon / 4× rectal cancer risk vs ~1950), which is the reasoning behind the move to age 45.
- **Cards: none written** — correct outcome, not a skipped step. The positive-stool-test delay fact is **already carded** (`c71013`, from the newer AGA 2022, 6-month threshold); age bands and test intervals are already carded from ACG/USPSTF; everything else ACS adds (strength vocabulary, modelling life-years-gained, incidence and prevalence figures, guideline version history) is on the *Cut* list. Card file's `page_updated:` bumped to 2026-11-10 to record the review.
- `needed-sources.md` row deleted — the ACS age-45 qualified recommendation it asked for is now on the page.

**Ingested 2 — `[[aga-2020-probiotics-technical-review]]`** (Preidis et al, *Gastroenterology* 2020;159:708–738; technical review / GRADE evidence synthesis behind [[aga-2020-probiotics]]):

- Source page created: the 8 PICO questions with the **overall certainty of evidence** each reached, the strain-level NEC effect sizes, the pouchitis evidence base, the IBS single-trial problem, and the scope exclusions.
- **The row's premise turned out to be wrong, and that is the finding.** It asked this document for "trial-level CFU doses and durations" for [[probiotics]]. Periprocedural: no routine antibiotic prophylaxis, antithrombotics managed as high-risk-for-bleeding **but the procedure may still proceed when they cannot be stopped**, no routine post-procedure medical therapy, refeeding <48 h, and **remove the LAMS before a later cholecystectomy** — which it does not make more complex than a percutaneous drain would.

- **Gaps stated plainly for the reader:** no data at all in small-bowel enteroscopy; limited data in therapeutic [[endoscopic-ultrasound|EUS]] and complex biliary/pancreatic work (the EUS trial was diagnostic-only); limited data in cirrhosis, including decompensated disease, acute-on-chronic liver failure and hepatic encephalopathy; nothing adequate on difficult-to-sedate patients (substance use disorders, marked obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, multiple psychoactive medications); **no US cost-effectiveness study**; and most trials Asian, using alfentanil/sufentanil where US practice uses fentanyl.

## [2026-10-31] ingest | PEGASYS label — the dose hepatitis D borrows, and the page it now has an owner on

**Source created:** [[pegasys-2023-peginterferon-alfa-2a-label]] — PEGASYS (peginterferon alfa-2a) injection, FDA prescribing information, rev. 12/2023, initial US approval 2002. DailyMed Set ID `d9290e5b-6d40-2318-e053-2995a90a9916`; `raw/Drug Labels/Pegasys Label.pdf` (1.2 MB, read with the Read tool).

**Why it qualified:** [[hepatitis-d]] carried an explicit flag — AASLD HBV guidance names the indication (elevated HDV RNA *and* elevated ALT → weekly subcutaneous peg-IFN-α for 12 months) but gives **no µg dose**. A drug hepatology prescribes, with the dose absent from every ingested guideline.

**The honest limit, recorded on every page it touches:** **the label does not mention hepatitis D at all.** Its indications are chronic hepatitis C and chronic hepatitis B. The **180 mcg subcutaneously weekly** figure reaches [[hepatitis-d]] as an **off-label extrapolation from the adult CHB regimen**, labelled as such — and the two durations disagree (AASLD 12 months vs the labelled 48 weeks), which the page states rather than silently picking one. The HDV treatment *trigger* is still unquantified; a product label cannot supply a patient-selection threshold, so the **EASL 2023 delta row stays on the download list**, narrowed to that half.

**New page created — [[peginterferon-alfa-2a]]** (`5-meds/`). Three pages referenced peg-IFN and none owned it, so the dose would otherwise have been written out three times. The page holds the regimen table, the dose-modification tables (ANC and platelet bands, creatinine clearance **<30 mL/min including hemodialysis → 135 mcg weekly**, the ALT-flare ladder, the depression ladder by severity and 8-week trajectory), the boxed warning, the contraindications, the monitoring schedule with the trials' acceptable baseline values, adverse effects, and the interactions.

**Pages updated:**

- [[hepatitis-d]] — dose line rewritten as the off-label extrapolation with the duration conflict named; the contraindication bullet now points at the drug page instead of restating it. The *"dose is not given"* half of its old flag is struck; the *"elevated is not quantified"* half stands.
- [[chronic-hepatitis-b]] — the one-line peginterferon bullet now links the drug page and carries **180 mcg weekly × 48 weeks**.
- [[hbv-nucleoside-analogs]] — its "peg-IFN is rarely used" line now links out for the dose.
- `index.md` rows for the source and the new med page; `needed-sources.md` Pegasys row deleted and the EASL delta row narrowed.

**Decision-critical content captured beyond the dose:**

- **Contraindications:** autoimmune hepatitis · **hepatic decompensation Child-Pugh >6 (class B and C)**, ≥6 in cirrhotic CHC/HIV · alpha-interferon hypersensitivity · neonates and infants (benzyl alcohol). Not recommended in solid organ transplant recipients; graft rejection reported.
- **Hepatitis B ALT flares are expected, not failure** — >10 × ULN in **12% HBeAg-negative and 18% HBeAg-positive** on treatment, 7% and 12% after stopping — with the discriminator that matters: **bilirubin, prothrombin time and albumin**, not the ALT value, separate an immune flare from incipient decompensation. Graded response captured (>5 × ULN → 135 mcg or hold; persistent >10 × ULN → consider stopping; progressive rise despite reduction, or with rising bilirubin or decompensation → **stop immediately**).
- **Two GI toxicities with their own stop rules:** ulcerative and hemorrhagic/ischemic **colitis within 12 weeks** of starting (abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, fever → stop immediately; resolves in 1–3 weeks) and **pancreatitis** — both sometimes fatal.
- **Azathioprine interaction:** pancytopenia 3–7 weeks into concomitant pegylated interferon/ribavirin plus azathioprine; stop all three and do not reintroduce the combination.

**No Anki cards** — guideline-sourced-cards-only. [[peginterferon-alfa-2a]] is label-sourced for every dose and threshold on it; the two guideline sources on the page contribute only the "rarely used" placement, which is not a card.

## [2026-10-31] ingest | VOWST (live-brpk) label — the oral spore product's prep sequence, and the follow-up the trial's headline stops short of

**Source created:** [[vowst-2025-live-brpk-label]] — VOWST (fecal microbiota spores, live-brpk) capsules, FDA prescribing information, rev. 2/2025, initial US approval 2023. DailyMed Set ID `99e5a37a-930c-4641-bcdd-7013ec1c15fe`; `raw/Drug Labels/Vowst Label.pdf` (192 KB, 12 pages, read with the Read tool, not `pdftotext`).

**Why it qualified:** the one row [[needed-sources]] carried for it, written off [[fmt]]'s own declared gap — [[aga-2024-fmt]] gives **no product dosing at all** and sends the reader to the package insert. The 2026-10-30 pass took the rectal product and narrowed the row to Vowst rather than deleting it; this closes the pair.

**What it adds that no ingested guideline prints:**

- **The preparation sequence**, which is the part that goes wrong at the bedside: finish the antibacterial course **2–4 days before** the first capsule · **296 mL (10 oz) magnesium citrate the day before and ≥8 h pre-dose** · **nothing by mouth but sips of water for ≥8 h** · Days 2 and 3 in the morning before breakfast.
- **Contraindications: none** — the label's own word, against the rectal product's one.
- **Storage is ordinary** — 2–25 °C, refrigerator or room temperature, never the freezer. No ultracold chain, which is a real difference in where the product can be held.
- **Per-capsule content 1×10⁶–3×10⁷ *Firmicutes* spore CFU** in 92 ± 4% glycerol in saline, and **mechanism of action not established** by the label's own statement.
- **The 12- and 24-week recurrence rates** the wiki did not carry: 12.4% vs 39.8% at 8 weeks (relative risk 0.32), **18.0% vs 46.2% at 12 weeks (0.40)**, **21.3% vs 47.3% at 24 weeks (0.46)**. The separation narrows and does not close.

**Pages updated:**

- [[fmt]] — new `### VOS — product dosing and administration (label)` section mirroring the RBL one: the regimen, the "no contraindications" line, the concurrent-antibacterial interaction, a `[!howto]` for the prep sequence, a `[!pitfall]` for the renal magnesium-citrate problem, storage, the adverse-reaction line with median durations, and the 8/12/24-week recurrence blockquote. The ECOSPOR III bullet was **rewritten rather than extended** — it now keeps the trial's efficacy and the *rationale* for the purge (vancomycin/fidaxomicin persist 5–7 days and inactivate the dose species) and hands the volume and timing to the label section, so the prep is stated once. The existing immunocompromise `[!pitfall]` gained VOS's "no contraindication at all".
- [[clostridioides-difficile]] — one line and a link, per *one home per fact*; product detail stays on the drug page.
- `index.md` row added; `needed-sources.md` Vowst row deleted.

**Contradictions / cautions recorded on the source page:**

- **"No contraindications" is not "no restrictions".** [[aga-2024-fmt]]'s severe-immunocompromise bar still governs selection, and the label's own trial exclusions agree — **neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count <500/mm³), toxic megacolon and small bowel ileus** were excluded, so no efficacy or safety figure here describes those patients.
- **Per-capsule vs per-dose CFU.** The label gives a per-capsule range; [[feuerstadt-2022-ser109-cdiff]] gives ≈3 × 10⁷ per dose. Different denominators, so neither is restated as the other — each is attributed to its own document.
- **The magnesium citrate prep has a renal caveat the guidelines lack.** The trials substituted **250 mL polyethylene glycol electrolyte solution** in impaired kidney function, and the label flags that as **not approved for this use**. Reported as a study practice, not an alternative.

**No Anki cards** — guideline-sourced-cards-only; a product label is not a guideline, CPU or consensus statement. Same disposition as the other eight label pages.

## [2026-10-30] ingest | REBYOTA (live-jslm) label — the rectal product's dose, technique and cold chain, none of which any guideline prints

**Source created:** [[rebyota-2022-live-jslm-label]] — FDA prescribing information, rev. 11/2022, via DailyMed. Fetched by this pass's daily source fetch.

**The gap it closes is stated on [[fmt]] in so many words:** "**FDA-approved products:** AGA gives **no dosing at all** and directs the reader to the **manufacturer's package insert**." That sentence has been on the page since the AGA 2024 ingest. The insert is now in `raw/`.

**Pages updated:**

- [[fmt]] — new `### RBL — product dosing and administration (label)` under the existing AGA-dosing subsection, deliberately placed so the guideline's "AGA specifies nothing" statement and the label's answer sit together. Added: the **single 150 mL rectal dose** and the **24–72 h post-antibiotic window**, the **Limitation of Use** (not indicated to *treat* CDI — only to prevent recurrence in adults ≥18 y), the single contraindication, the transmissible-agent and **food-allergen** warnings, the **8-week oral-antibiotic avoidance** counselling rule, the persistent-diarrhea reporting definition, the adverse-reaction rates, the specific-population statements, and the **cold chain** (ultracold −60 to −90 °C or 2–8 °C ≤5 days *including thaw time*; thaw ~24 h in a refrigerator, never with heat, never refreeze; administration set 10–34 °C and never frozen).
- **Technique reached the page as a `[!howto]`, not as screenshots.** The label's Figures 1–10 are procedural illustrations rather than a decision algorithm, and every element is text-expressible, so they were recreated natively per Style Guide (*Tables: recreate, don't screenshot* — same logic): positioning, **12 cm (5 in) insertion angled toward the umbilicus**, **gravity flow only**, retain position **up to 15 min**. A `[!pitfall]` carries the three stated ways to lose the dose (tube sagging or looping, squeezing the bag, hanging it from an IV stand) and the label's note that residual product in the tube is **expected**.
- **One existing line tightened:** the page gave the RBL schedule as "1–3 days after completing antimicrobials" from [[aga-2026-cdiff-ibd]]. The label's **24–72 hours** is the same window stated precisely; the AGA phrasing is kept with the label's figure beside it rather than overwritten, since the guideline remains the authority for *when in the course* and the label for *how*.
- **Corroboration, not a new claim:** the **1×10⁸–5×10¹⁰ CFU/mL** per-dose content was already on the page second-hand through [[aga-2024-fmt]] quoting the insert. The insert confirms it verbatim, and adds >1×10⁵ CFU/mL *Bacteroides* and ≤5.97 g PEG 3350.

**Contradictions and limits surfaced (three, all on the page):**

- ⚠ **Efficacy splits by timepoint.** 8-week treatment success **70.6% vs 57.5%** (difference 13.1 points, 95% credible interval 2.3–24.0; posterior probability of superiority **0.991** against a pre-set 0.975) — but **6-month sustained clinical response 65.5% vs 56.5%, difference 9.1%, 95% CI −3.6% to 21.7%, not significant.** This is the **opposite pattern** to [[feuerstadt-2022-ser109-cdiff]]'s 88% vs 60% sustained response for the oral spore product. The two were **never compared head to head** and the page says so; neither result licenses a claim about the other product.
- ⚠ **Label silence is not permission.** RBL's only contraindication is component allergy — it carries **no immunocompromise restriction**. [[aga-2024-fmt]] independently bars microbiota-based therapy in severe immunocompromise and allows only conventional FMT in mild/moderate. These are different instruments, not a conflict; the guideline governs patient selection and the wiki does not weaken it on the label's silence. Captured as a `[!pitfall]` because it is exactly the inference a reader would otherwise draw.
- ⚠ **Mechanism of action is unestablished by the label's own statement**, and no nonclinical toxicology studies were conducted. Noted so no mechanistic account is later attributed to this source.
- ⚠ **Trial population excludes the comorbidities most often asked about** — celiac disease, IBD, IBS and chronic diarrhea were excluded from both randomized studies, so the efficacy figures do not describe those patients. Stated beside the figures.

**Index:** row added under `sources/`.

**No Anki cards** — product label, so *Guideline-sourced cards only* excludes all of it. [[fmt]]'s card file will read as stale against the page's new `updated:` date; the staleness is cosmetic, exactly as on 2026-10-30's earlier card pass, because every fact added here is label-sourced and uncardable.

**Download list:** the Rebyota row is **not deleted** — it reads "Rebyota / Vowst labels", and **Vowst is still outstanding**. Row narrowed to Vowst alone rather than removed.

Counting failures alone systematically under-grades.

  - **[[fish]] — the declared gap is closed, and it was the sharpest one left.** The page said in its own text that *"neither ACG 2023 nor ASGE 2023 defines polysomy cytogenetically — neither states how many cells or which probe gains are required to call a result polysomic."* **Figure 3 is now on the page as a native table**: polysomy = **≥3 copies of ≥2 probes** (excluding tetrasomy), cut-off **≥4 cells on the entire slide**; tetrasomy ≥10%, single-locus gain with 9p21 loss ≥5%, homozygous 9p21 loss ≥5%, single-locus gain of 1q21/8q24/9p21 ≥8%, of 7p12 ≥10%, all of a 100-cell enumeration.
  - ⚠ **Two things on that table change how a report is read, and both are now stated.** **Only polysomy is a positive result** — every other abnormality is *equivocal*, neither negative nor positive. And the **polysomy threshold is an absolute count, not a percentage**: ≥4 cells anywhere on the slide regardless of how many were counted, unlike every equivocal category. A `[!pearl]` carries that, because misreading it as "4%" sets the bar far too high.
  - **A second gap the page did not know it had: which probe set.** Biliary FISH may be run with **UroVysion** (CEP 3/7/17 + 9p21, designed for **bladder cancer**) or the **pancreatobiliary set (1q21, 7p12, 8q24, 9p21)**, and head-to-head on the same 183 brushings they differ by ~19 percentage points of cancer detection — **64.7% vs 45.9%** sensitivity at 92.9% vs 90.8% specificity (routine cytology 18.8% / 100%). A `[!pitfall]` says what follows: **"FISH negative" does not mean the same thing everywhere** — check the probe set before treating it as reassurance.
  - **The reading rules travelled with the table**, because two readers otherwise produce different numbers: **100 consecutive epithelial cells**, at most **5 from any disomic group**; a post-enumeration scan whose **polysomic cells are added but whose non-polysomic findings are disregarded**; polysomy wins over homozygous 9p21 loss in the same cell; **9p21 loss as the overlap discriminator** (unexpected in benign cells, so it separates one abnormal nucleus from two overlapping benign ones); **≥100 cells for adequacy**.

But it is **tier 2 and compares two assays, not PSC against non-PSC strictures**, so both tier-1 guidelines keep the page and the contradiction block stands. **Added beside it:** the multivariable **odds ratio 0.18 for PSC** is the **lower cancer prevalence of a surveillance population**, not worse accuracy — the likeliest misreading now that the figure is on the page.

**Ingested (file 1): [[linzess-2026-linaclotide-label|LINZESS (Linaclotide) Capsules — FDA Prescribing Information]] — this pass's fetched item, so it goes first; it also corrects something the wiki had wrong.**

- ⚠ **A wrong statement deleted, not merely supplemented.** [[linaclotide]] carried the note *"the pediatric contraindication is on the FDA label"*, which reads as excluding all children. The contraindication is **age <2 y only** — above that floor linaclotide is **indicated**: **≥7 y for IBS-C at 145 µg daily** and **≥2 y for functional constipation at 72 µg daily**. The page now prints all four dose-by-population rows and a pitfall box saying so explicitly.
- **The gap the row named is closed in both directions.** **Exactly two contraindications** (age <2 y; known or suspected mechanical GI obstruction), and **no renal and no hepatic adjustment** — with the reason, which is what makes it safe to rely on: linaclotide is metabolised **inside the gut lumen** and plasma concentrations are below the limit of quantitation at 72, 145 and 290 µg, so area under the curve, maximum concentration and half-life **cannot be calculated at all**.
- ⚠ **The boxed warning is mechanistic, not statistical**, and that matters for how far it generalises: in neonatal mice a single clinically relevant adult-equivalent dose caused **death from dehydration within 24 h** through age-dependent elevated GC-C agonism, and tolerability rises steeply with age (10 µg/kg/day killed neonatal mice; 2-week-olds tolerated 50 but died at a single 100 µg/kg; 3-week-olds tolerated 100 but died at 600). A GC-C ontogeny study in **99 children** found **no age-dependent trend in intestinal GC-C expression from 2 to <18 y** but **insufficient data below 2 y** — which is exactly where the line was drawn.
- **Severe diarrhea is dose-stratified, and the page previously had only the pooled figure.** **2%** at 145 µg or 290 µg vs **<1%** at 72 µg, majority starting **within the first 2 weeks**; the action rule is **suspend dosing and rehydrate**, and post-marketing reports give the consequence — severe diarrhea with dizziness, syncope, hypotension and **hypokalemia or hyponatremia** requiring hospitalisation or intravenous fluid. Added with it: the **long-term tolerability ceiling** nobody had on file — at 290 µg daily for up to 18 months, **29%** of 2,147 IBS-C and **27%** of 1,129 CIC patients had the dose reduced or suspended for adverse reactions.
- **Administration is now a usable procedure, not one sentence.** The page had "take without food, ≥30 min before the first meal". It now carries the missed-dose rule (**skip it, never two at once**), the swallow-whole rule, and the three capsule-opening routes as a table — applesauce (1 teaspoonful, consume immediately), water (**~30 mL, swirl ≥20 s**, repeat), and **nasogastric/gastrostomy tube** (**10 mL per 10 s**, then flush ≥10 mL). Boxed as a pearl: **the beads do not dissolve** — the drug is coated on their surface, so beads left in the cup or tube do not cost you any of the dose.
- **Propagation was deliberately one page.** [[linaclotide]] owns dosing and labelled safety (one-owner rule); [[chronic-idiopathic-constipation]] and [[irritable-bowel-syndrome]] were left untouched, since nothing on the label changes their algorithms and both already link the drug page. Adult doses on the page from [[aga-acg-2023-constipation]], [[acg-2020-ibs]] and [[aga-2022-ibs-c]] **match the label exactly** — no source-priority conflict to resolve.

**Ingested (file 3): [[ascrs-2017-rectal-prolapse|ASCRS 2017 Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Treatment of Rectal Prolapse]] — second in the hand-off order, and it answers the question [[rectal-prolapse]] had been declining to answer.**

- **All 16 recommendations captured** with the document's own GRADE labels. ⚠ **The document numbers within each section, restarting at 1** (Evaluation 1–3, Nonoperative 1, Abdominal 1–2, Posterior Dissection 1, Suture Rectopexy 1–3, Posterior Mesh 1–2, Ventral 1, Additional Abdominal 1, Perineal 1–2) — so the source page reproduces the section headings and keeps the document's own numbers rather than inventing a flat 1–16 scheme.
- ⚠ **It is older than [[acg-2021-anorectal-disorders]], and that was enforced rather than assumed.** ACG 2021 is newer in the same tier and governs every overlap — its conditional statement and its laparoscopic-rectopexy preference stay as the page's headline, and ACG's **27%** Altemeier recurrence stays beside ASCRS's **16%–30% at 2 years** rather than replacing it. ASCRS adds strictly below the level ACG addresses; **nothing was overwritten**, which is the whole point of the older-source rule.
- **The gap the page declared is closed in its own words.** It read: *"None of the sources here grades prolapse severity (e.g. by length of prolapsed segment) or covers non-operative/conservative management."* **Non-operative management is now a section** — prolapse **cannot** be corrected nonoperatively (no reports of resolution on medical therapy alone, 2C); medicine palliates with fiber and stool softeners, **topical table sugar to reduce edema and assist reduction of an incarcerated prolapse**, skin care, and **pre-treating the incontinence before surgery**, which gave better postoperative continence. **The severity-grading half is narrowed, not closed** — ASCRS supplies no staging scale either, only the **<5 cm** threshold selecting the Delorme procedure, and the note now says exactly that.
- ⚠ **A pitfall box for the advice patients most often get wrong:** watchful waiting costs something. Medically-managed patients **develop irreversible fecal incontinence**, and **prolapse left untreated beyond 4 years** carries higher recurrence after eventual repair — the document extends this **explicitly to the elderly**, who are the ones usually counselled to wait.
- **The two selection rules are the decision content, and they were entirely missing.** **Prolapse + FI → correct the prolapse first**, because continence often improves once it is gone — and in that patient **lateral-stalk division is desirable**, trading constipation for lower recurrence (2B). Conversely **coexisting constipation or dyssynergia disqualifies** posterior rectal mobilization, lateral-ligament transection and levatorplasty, and **severe preoperative constipation calls for more than a suture rectopexy**. With it, the number that explains why: suture rectopexy alone worsens constipation in **≥50%** of the already-constipated and creates it de novo in **≈15%**.
- **One hard technical rule and one refusal.** **Posterior mobilization without a rectopexy is not recommended (1B)** — an RCT found an **8-fold rise in recurrence** with mobilization alone — and **rectopexy is a key component of the abdominal approach (1A)**. But the document **explicitly declines to rank posterior against anterior repair (1C, insufficient evidence)**, so the page asserts no winner either.
- **A six-row operation table built from the document's recurrence figures**, including the two that change counselling: suture rectopexy looks good at **3%–9% at 2 years** but reaches **29% at 10 years**, and **levatorplasty cut Altemeier recurrence from 21% to 7%**. Each row carries its own caveat — resection rectopexy **risks ischemic bowel after a failed perineal rectosigmoidectomy** and **resolves FI less often**; ventral mesh rectopexy ⚠ **"has yet to gain full acceptance in the United States"** despite European preference, which the document says itself and which decides what a US patient is actually offered.
- **Pre-referral workup added to Diagnostics:** **colonoscopy should typically precede prolapse surgery** (1B — a neoplasm can be the lead point, the population is older, and a finding may change the operative plan), plus **selective urodynamics / urogynecologic examination** when anterior-compartment or urinary symptoms are present, so both compartments can be repaired in one operation. Also the bedside escalation when the prolapse will not appear (strain on a toilet ± enema or rectal balloon, inspect sitting or squatting, or **have the patient photograph it at home**).
- **An associations table added to Assessment** — FI **50%–75%**, constipation **25%–50%**, pudendal neuropathy **up to 50%**, urinary incontinence **20%–35%**, vaginal vault prolapse **≈15%–30%**, anterior solitary rectal ulcer on proctoscopy **10%–15%** — because every one of them is an input to the operative choice above, not background colour.
- **Propagation was one page by design.** [[rectal-prolapse]] owns every one of these decisions; [[fecal-incontinence]], [[chronic-constipation]] and [[colonoscopy]] were left untouched rather than given duplicate copies, per one-home.
- **`needed-sources.md`: row deleted** (the row's remaining half named exactly this document).
- **Cards: eligible, not written this pass** — tier-1 society guideline; card writing belongs to the nightly card pass.

**Ingested (file 4): [[caps-2020-pancreatic-surveillance|CAPS 2020: Management of Patients with Increased Risk for Familial Pancreatic Cancer]] — third in the hand-off order, and the document [[pancreatic-cancer-screening]] had been naming by author in two standing gap notes.**

- **Both declared gaps are closed, and the notes deleted rather than re-flagged.** The page read, in two places, that the answer was "in the CAPS consortium recommendations (Goggins 2020)" — once for the **lesion strata behind [[aga-2020-pancreas-cancer-screening|AGA 2020]]'s surveillance-interval ladder**, which AGA names (low-risk / indeterminate / high-risk) but **never defines**, and once for **operative thresholds in a high-risk individual**, which [[asge-2022-pancreatic-cancer-screening|ASGE 2022]] does not address at all. Both now have tables.
- **The interval strata, as findings rather than labels:** 12 months for no abnormality, a cyst without worrisome features, pancreatic lobulation, or a **<1 cm** non-functioning neuroendocrine tumour; **3–6 months** for a CDKN2A p16 carrier with mild main-duct dilation or a stricture without a mass; **3 months** for a solid lesion of uncertain significance or a main-duct stricture when surgery is not planned — the last two **grade 1**, the strongest action grade in the document.
- ⚠ **The operative thresholds, including the one that was voted *down*.** Resect a solid lesion at **≥10 mm** (91.2%) or **≥5 mm** (77.9%), both grade 1 — but resecting **regardless of size** reached only 64.7% and is **grade 4, "probably don't do it"**. That negative is as decision-relevant as the positives and is printed as such. An **IPMN in a high-risk individual** is resected for any of **six grade-1 features**, including a **main pancreatic duct ≥10 mm** — ⚠ flagged on the page as the **high-risk-individual** criteria, explicitly not to be copied onto [[pancreatic-cysts]], which has its own sporadic-cyst set.
- **Test selection turned out to be the quiet net-new content.** CAPS grades **CT 4 and abdominal ultrasound 5** for routine surveillance at baseline *and* follow-up — CT has a role only **after** a finding (a solid lesion, or a duct stricture without a mass) — and restricts **CA 19-9 to individuals with worrisome features on imaging** while making **fasting glucose and/or HbA1c routine**. None of that was on the page.
- ⚠ **It is older than ASGE 2022, and that was enforced row by row rather than assumed.** A new resolution table records each contact: CAPS **requires** an affected first-degree relative for BRCA2 and PALB2 where **ASGE requires none** (superseded, both printed, because the older rule is still in wide use); CAPS puts **Peutz-Jeghers at 40** against ASGE's **35** (superseded; a line was added to [[peutz-jeghers-syndrome]] so a reader meeting the CAPS number knows why the page says 35); ATM, Lynch and CDKN2A are **concordant**; and CAPS is **net-new** on hereditary pancreatitis — **age 40 or 20 years after the first pancreatitis attack**, a post-attack clause ASGE does not have.
- ⚠ **Three places the document declines to answer, recorded as non-answers rather than smoothed over** — the same failure family the memory file flags. **BRCA1's family-history criterion reached only 69.6%**, below CAPS's own 75% threshold, so it is **graded 3, no recommendation** (surveillance of BRCA1 carriers itself did reach consensus); **no consensus on the age to stop surveillance**, so AGA 2020's stop rule stands unchallenged; and **no consensus on whether or how to alternate MRI/MRCP and EUS**, even though Table 3 lists alternation as the follow-up strategy — so **no alternation schedule was written onto the page**.

The rest live in **online supplementary table S2, which is not in `raw/`**. Nothing was copied to [[pancreatic-cysts]], [[hereditary-pancreatitis]] or [[fammm-syndrome]].

**17 distinct** — each pair separated by a different drug, formulation, population, threshold or decision: ileal-release budesonide (Crohn's) vs multimatrix budesonide (ulcerative colitis); large-balloon dilation >=12 mm after sphincterotomy vs 8 mm papillary dilation without one; artifactual outflow obstruction in a surgery-naive esophagus vs post-fundoplication obstruction; the 5-day definition of variceal treatment failure vs salvage-versus-rescue TIPS; CDH1 cascade-testing age 16 vs prophylactic gastrectomy after 20; universal tumour testing in colorectal cancer vs immunohistochemistry-first in Lynch screening; 72 hours of high-dose proton pump inhibitor vs twice-daily dosing through day 14; Rome V 1-of-3 abnormal tests to diagnose dyssynergia vs 2-of-3 to call constipation refractory; the two halves of the Barrett's ESD-over-EMR list, which cannot be one note inside the bullet and cloze caps; and the rest.

- Kept **distinct** deliberately: tapping new hepatic hydrothorax vs tapping new ascites. The answer reads the same ("tap every one of them") but the population and the procedure differ — thoracentesis for occult spontaneous bacterial empyema, paracentesis for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis — so they are two decisions, unlike the single shared culture technique merged above.

**Resume markers:** `grep -rn "ingest: partial" wiki/` → hits only in `wiki/log.md` prose. **No source page is mid-ingest**, so this pass starts new files rather than finishing one.

**Ingested (file 1): [[bsg-2017-common-bile-duct-stones|BSG 2017: Updated Guideline on the Management of Common Bile Duct Stones]] — first in the previous pass's hand-off order, and the only document in the corpus that defines a "difficult" stone.**

- **Every statement captured.** The document **numbers none of its recommendations**; its Summary of Recommendations prints **31 blocks**, two of which carry two separately-graded clauses, so the source page numbers **33** and says the numbering is the wiki's. Each keeps the document's own provenance label (`2008` / `2008, amended 2016` / `2016` / `New 2016`), evidence grade and strength.
- ⚠ **Strength does not track quality in this document, and it says so.** Where evidence was weak but group consensus was clear, the panel still issued a **strong** recommendation. Recorded on the source page so a future pass does not "correct" a Low-quality/strong pairing.
- ⚠ **One wording discrepancy inside the document itself:** the prohibitive-operative-risk alternative (sphincterotomy + endoscopic clearance instead of cholecystectomy) is printed as *suggested* in the Summary of Recommendations and *recommended* in the body, with the same Low/weak grade both times. Both printed, neither silently chosen.
- **The gap this closes.** [[cholangioscopy]] carried a standing flag that **"difficult" is not defined by any ingested guideline**. It now carries both definitions side by side, because they are not the same definition: [[asge-2015-ercp-benign-biliary|ASGE 2015]] applies the word *before* cholangioscopy (not removable after sphincterotomy ± balloon or mechanical lithotripsy → go to cholangioscopy), BSG 2017 applies "difficult **stone disease**" only once **cholangioscopy has also failed** → percutaneous extraction or open duct exploration (major complications **3.6%–6.8%**). Same word, one rung apart, different next move. The flag sentence is deleted, not re-flagged. `needed-sources.md` row deleted.
- **Figure 1 reached the page as a Mermaid diagram, not a screenshot** — `pdftoppm` is permission-blocked in this session, but the Read tool renders the PDF page, so the algorithm was read off page 7 and recreated on [[choledocholithiasis]] with the node text intact (including the branch most pathways leave implicit: a negative MRCP/EUS loops back to *consider alternative diagnosis*, and persisting suspicion at **low** likelihood still earns an MRCP or EUS).
- **The decision inputs behind the probability strata are now printed, not just the strata.** The wiki asserted high/intermediate/low from [[asge-2019-choledocholithiasis|ASGE 2019]]'s criteria table; BSG supplies the measured performance — ultrasound sensitivity **0.73** / specificity **0.91**, and the post-test probabilities at three pre-test probabilities, plus bilirubin and alkaline-phosphatase cut-points. ⚠ **The pitfall box the numbers justify:** a negative ultrasound leaves a **3%** stone risk at 9.5% pre-test probability but **37%** at 65.8% — which is why normal results do not preclude further investigation.
- **MRCP vs EUS, with the caveat that matters:** at a median pre-test probability of **41%**, sensitivity **0.95 vs 0.93** and specificity **0.97 vs 0.96**, with no clear superiority head-to-head — but **those figures do not transfer** to low or high pre-test probability. Choice is by patient factors (pacemaker/clips/claustrophobia/obesity → EUS; availability, intrahepatic ducts, altered anatomy, reviewable images → MRCP), which are now listed.
- ⚠ **Extract the stone even when it is small.** GallRiks (34,200 intraoperative cholangiograms, 11.6% with a stone): unfavourable outcome **25.3%** left in situ vs **12.7%** scheduled for extraction, and the benefit **persisted for stones <4 mm** (8.9% vs 15.9%). Boxed as a pearl — with the document's own counterweight beside it, that **the natural history of an incidentally found stone in an asymptomatic patient has never been studied**, so that advice rests on symptomatic-patient evidence and expert opinion.
- **Propagation (4 further pages), split by who owns what:**
  - [[choledocholithiasis]] — the Figure 1 algorithm, the accuracy tables, the natural-history pearl, **stent-as-definitive-treatment** (on-demand exchange **36% cholangitis / 8% mortality** vs elective 3-monthly **8% / 2%**), **LBDE as a co-equal option** to perioperative ERCP with the transductal/primary-closure detail, and a new **after-duct-clearance gall-bladder decision** subsection (cholecystectomy mortality **14.1% vs 7.9%**; ⚠ an *empty* gall bladder is a different question, recurrence **5.9%–11.3%** vs **15%–23.7%**, and wait-and-see may reasonably be discussed there).

**Ingested (file 1): [[gattex-2025-teduglutide-label|GATTEX (Teduglutide) — FDA Prescribing Information]] — the dose [[glp-2-agonists]] had been declaring missing since July.**

- The page's `## Dosing & Monitoring` section consisted of a single bullet saying the AGA clinical practice updates give no dose, no monitoring and no adverse-effect detail. It now carries the real numbers: **0.05 mg/kg once daily subcutaneously**, adults and children ≥1 y alike, with the one adjustment — **halve to 0.025 mg/kg at eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m²**. No hepatic adjustment at Child-Pugh A/B, **not studied at C**, **no contraindications**.
- ⚠ **A preparation ceiling that is a real prescribing constraint:** the 5 mg vial reconstitutes to 10 mg/mL and **only 0.38 mL (3.8 mg) can be withdrawn**, so a patient over roughly 76 kg needs **more than one vial per dose**. Easy to miss and nowhere else in the corpus.
- **The most useful content is the endoscopic surveillance program, and it is a gastroenterologist's job no ingested society document specifies.** Colonoscopy **and** upper endoscopy with polypectomy **within the 6 months before starting**; repeat **at the end of year 1**; then **no less frequently than every 5 years** if no polyp was found. Labs (bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, lipase, amylase) at baseline and **every 6 months**. **A GI cancer diagnosed on therapy means stopping the drug.** Children get annual fecal occult blood testing instead, with scopes at 1 year and every 5 years. Captured as a table on [[glp-2-agonists]].
- **Two adverse events interrupt therapy, and the response differs.** **Intestinal or stomal obstruction — 4% at the recommended dose, 9% at twice it, 0% on placebo** → hold and restart once it resolves (2 of 8 extension-study episodes needed endoscopic dilation, 1 needed surgery). **Fluid overload / congestive heart failure** (edema 10% vs 3%, CHF 2 cases) → **adjust parenteral support** rather than reflexively stopping, because it follows from the enhanced absorption the drug is given for. Boxed as a pitfall.
- **Stoma complications 42% (13/31) vs 14% (3/22) on placebo** — the single largest between-arm difference in the label and directly relevant to [[ostomy-management]].
- **Anti-teduglutide antibodies reach 48% by month 30** (54% at 12 months in children) **with no observed loss of efficacy, no pharmacokinetic change and no adverse-event association** — recorded explicitly so a rising titre is not read as a reason to stop.
- ⚠ **One wording difference surfaced rather than reconciled.** [[short-bowel-syndrome]] says teduglutide is "contraindicated with active gastrointestinal malignancy" ([[aga-2022-short-bowel-syndrome]]); the label lists **no formal contraindication** but requires **discontinuation** if GI cancer is diagnosed on therapy. The guideline governs the page under *Source priority*; the labelled wording is stated beside it.

**Ingested (file 2): [[sages-2013-hiatal-hernia|SAGES 2013 Guidelines for the Management of Hiatal Hernia]] — the document SAGES 2024 complements, and the context [[hiatal-hernia]] was citing 2024 without.**

- First in the 2026-10-25 hand-off pick order, and tier-1. **All 28 statements captured** with the document's own GRADE symbols (⊕ very low → ⊕⊕⊕⊕ high) and strong/weak strength, condensed but unchanged in direction, population and force.
- ⚠ **One statement carries no grade at all, and it is the mesh one.** Statement 11 recommends mesh for **short-term** recurrence reduction (⊕⊕⊕, strong); statement 12 says the **long-term data are inadequate to recommend either for or against** mesh at the hiatus — **ungraded, uniquely in the document**. Both are reproduced side by side rather than reconciled, and the pages say the **current** society position is [[sages-2024-hiatal-hernia-surgery|SAGES 2024]]'s **no recommendation**. Same failure family the memory file records for `asge-2020-endoscopic-removal` — the fix is to print what the document prints, including the absence of a grade.
- **The three mesh RCTs are carried with their numbers, because the directions disagree across follow-up:** **22%→0%** (defect >8 cm, 3.3 y), **26%→8%** (1 y), and **59%→54%, p=0.7** at **4.8 y with both arms over 50%**. **No mesh-related complications in any of the three.** A table of early wins and a null long-term trial is the whole mesh story and reads wrong if flattened to "mesh helps".
- **Statements 8, 10, 16 and 19 each bundle two differently-graded clauses** (approach: ⊕⊕⊕⊕ strong *and* ⊕⊕ strong; sac: dissect ⊕⊕ strong *then* excise ⊕⊕ weak; length: ⊕⊕ weak *achieved by* ⊕⊕⊕⊕ strong; gastropexy-alone: ⊕⊕ weak *but formal repair preferred* ⊕⊕⊕⊕ strong). Kept bundled with both grades visible, since splitting them loses which half is strong.
- **The decision content is the natural history, and it is why "repair every PEH" is no longer the rule.** Progression asymptomatic→symptomatic **≈14%/y**; risk of needing **emergency** surgery **<2%/y**; emergency-repair mortality **0–5.4%** in recent series against an average of about **17%**; and decision modelling suggesting elective repair of a completely asymptomatic PEH **may decrease quality-adjusted life expectancy at age ≥65**. Reserve it for gastric outlet obstruction, severe reflux or anemia, or possible strangulation.
- ⚠ **A PEH does not present like reflux, and that is the commonest way it is missed** — heartburn and regurgitation are *uncommon*; the patient reports postprandial chest fullness or dyspnea (pulmonary compression, reduced forced vital capacity), or pain relieved by vomiting. **Iron deficiency anemia in up to 50%.** Boxed as a pitfall on [[hiatal-hernia]].
- **Propagation (3 further pages), split by who owns what:**
  - [[hiatal-hernia]] — type distribution (>95% type I; >90% of PEH are type III; type II least common), the inconsistent "giant PEH" definition, the elastin mechanism, the PEH symptom pitfall, the **indication table by type** (including repair of every hernia found at a bariatric operation), the natural-history numbers, and a new **`#### Gastric volvulus — the emergency`** subsection (organoaxial vs mesenteroaxial, **Borchardt triad**, decompress-before-investigating, gastric viability). Its *What the guidelines deliberately do not say* section gains the mesh history and the **>5.6 cm² hiatal-surface-area recurrence predictor** — which is a recurrence predictor, **not** the size threshold for repair that still does not exist in either document.
  - [[antireflux-surgery]] — the whole operative layer, as a new **`### Hiatal Hernia Repair — the Steps that Define an Adequate Operation`** table plus a postoperative subsection: approach, sac dissection and excision, GEJ below the diaphragm, **≥2–3 cm of intra-abdominal esophagus**, mandatory fundoplication in type I repair, no-tailoring-to-manometry, gastropexy (and gastropexy-alone's **22% radiologic recurrence at 3 months**), revisional surgery, Collis gastroplasty and its non-peristaltic neoesophagus, recurrence predictors, the mesh pitfall box, and the postoperative course (**early dysphagia up to 50%**, expected **10–15 lb** weight loss, evaluate **>20 lb**, no routine contrast study in the asymptomatic).
  - [[bariatric-surgery]] — repair every hiatal hernia detected during a bariatric operation, how they are detected (dimpling anterior to the esophagus), and the band-series reoperation benefit.
- **Deliberately not duplicated.** The type I–IV table was already on [[hiatal-hernia]] from the 2024 guideline and was not rewritten; the 2024 fundoplication/mesh/asymptomatic/Roux-en-Y answers keep their existing section and were not restated from the 2013 text.

**Ingested (file 3): [[asge-2014-dysphagia|ASGE 2014 The Role of Endoscopy in the Evaluation and Management of Dysphagia]] — the general-purpose dilation anchor the wiki never had, and it closes a gap [[esophageal-stricture]] had declared on itself.**

- Second in the hand-off pick order, and a `needed-sources.md` row in its own right. **Still the current US document** on both dysphagia and esophageal dilation — there is no newer American guideline on either. **All 8 recommendations captured** with the document's own GRADE symbols.
- **Two definition sets that existed nowhere in the corpus, and both are decision gates:**
  - **Simple** stricture — short, **symmetric or concentric**, **≥12 mm**, endoscope-traversable — versus **complex** — **>2 cm long, angulated or irregular, <12 mm**, higher recurrence *and* higher adverse-event rate, and the trigger for **wire-guided dilation under fluoroscopy or a through-the-scope balloon** (⊕⊕⊕○).
  - **Refractory** — **cannot be dilated to 14 mm over 5 sessions at 2-week intervals** — versus **recurrent** — **cannot maintain 14 mm for 4 weeks** once achieved. ⚠ **Neither applies to an inflammatory stricture or to neuromuscular dysphagia**, which is the half of the definition that stops a clinician from dilating something that will not respond.
- **The dose–symptom scale behind all of it: regular diet at 18 mm · modified diet at 15 mm · dysphagia at ≤13 mm**, with the endoscope's own ~9 mm diameter as the bedside estimate (and the guideline's own caveat that this is subjective).
- ⚠ **The "rule of 3" is stated and disclaimed in the same paragraph** — "accepted but not formally studied for its safety" — **does not apply to balloon dilation**, and **increments >3 mm may be safe in simple strictures**. Written up as a pitfall box that carries the disclaimer, not as a rule.
- ⚠ **Two practices the document argues against, both easy to get wrong:** **empiric large-bore (50F) dilation of dysphagia with a normal endoscopy** repeatedly failed to improve dysphagia scores and may not be worth the perforation risk, especially with undiagnosed eosinophilic esophagitis; and **antibiotic prophylaxis purely to prevent endocarditis**, despite bacteremia of 12%–22%.
- ⚠ **The operator is a measured risk factor** — perforation was **4× more frequent** when the endoscopist had done **fewer than 500 previous diagnostic upper endoscopies**. Also: **a normal chest radiograph does not exclude perforation**.
- **Closed a gap the wiki had stated plainly.** [[esophageal-stricture]] said in reader-facing text that *"no ingested source covers Schatzki ring or anastomotic strictures; both are left out here rather than stated without support."* Both are now on the page from this document — including the **distinction from a peptic stricture** (a Schatzki ring is a diaphragm-like web at the squamocolumnar junction marking the proximal margin of a hiatal hernia, and **may disappear with air insufflation at endoscopy**, so barium swallow detects it better), the **EoE association that warrants biopsy**, the **9%–48%** anastomotic-stricture rate after esophagectomy with its risk factors, and post-radiation strictures. **That sentence is deleted, not re-flagged.**
- **Propagation (3 further pages), with technique on the procedure page and classification on the disease page:**
  - [[esophageal-dilation]] — the page had only EoE-specific guidance. It gains the **three dilator families and their mechanics** (⚠ **a larger balloon needs *less* pressure and carries a *higher* perforation risk**; a shorter-taper bougie is safer), wire-guided and Maloney technique, the rule-of-3 pitfall, the empiric-50F pitfall, fasting and stasis rules, the diet-by-diameter table, and a new **`## When Dilation Alone Is Not Enough`** section: refractory/recurrent definitions, **triamcinolone 40 mg/mL, 0.2–0.5 mL into 4 quadrants** with its effect sizes (**50F vs 40F**, **13% vs 60%** repeat dilations, **167 vs 23 days** between them), the stent data as a pitfall box, and self-bougienage.
  - [[esophageal-stricture]] — simple/complex and refractory/recurrent as its `### Classification / Typing`, the four new etiologies in the differential, and per-type expectations under Therapeutics.
  - [[dysphagia]] — **EGD in suspected *oropharyngeal* dysphagia** with a complete upper-esophageal-sphincter and hypopharynx examination (the schema had none), plus the **amenable-vs-not-amenable-to-dilation** table and the 13 mm threshold.
- **Deliberately not propagated: the achalasia section.** Pneumatic dilation balloon sizes, the graded 30→35 mm safety data, the dilation-vs-myotomy trial and meta-analysis, and the manometric-subtype response rates are all **superseded by [[asge-2020-achalasia]] and [[acg-2020-achalasia]]** — same tier, 6 years newer. Recorded on the source page as what the 2014 position was; [[achalasia]] is untouched.

- **`needed-sources.md`:** the ASGE 2014 dysphagia row **deleted** (ingested). The SAGES hiatal-hernia row **deleted** as well — both its documents are now in — but **one part of it was genuinely still open**, so a **Cameron lesions** row was written in its place, in the descriptive-gaps section: neither SAGES document mentions them, nor does any GERD, bleeding or anemia guideline in `raw/`. **No specific article is named**, because a narrative review would fail *What belongs on the download list*. **Net: 4 rows deleted, 1 added.**
- **Cards: eligible, not written this pass** — same reason as file 2.

It was not — yesterday's health check found it with **zero inbound links from any page**, and [[barretts-esophagus]] contained **no mention of a capsule sponge, Cytosponge, transnasal endoscopy or esophageal capsule at all**. Finishing it outranks starting a fourth new file (*finish the unfinished first*), and it is a propagation job, not a link fix — adding the slug to a `sources:` line without the content would only have made the orphan count look better.
- **[[barretts-esophagus]] gains a new `#### Nonendoscopic and Alternative-Endoscopic Screening Tools` subsection** — a four-row table of capsule sponge, transnasal endoscopy, video capsule and the unvalidated tools, with device mechanics, performance and the limit that kills each one.
- ⚠ **The quoted capsule-sponge sensitivity needs its qualifier and now has it.** BEST2 intention-to-treat sensitivity is **79.9%**, rising to **87.2%** with ≥3 cm circumferential disease and **89.7%** on a repeat procedure. The **91.5%** figure often cited came from a **73-patient enriched population with inadequate samples excluded**, and the source says so itself.
- ⚠ **Transnasal endoscopy's biopsy shortfall (83% vs 100%) is technical, not inherent** — investigators could not pass the 5.8 mm biopsy-capable sheath and used a 4.7 mm sheath with no biopsy channel. Recorded that way, since "TNE can't biopsy" is the wrong conclusion. **It is still not adequate for dysplasia surveillance** (optical quality, no virtual chromoendoscopy).
- **The economics are the real teaching point and are on the page:** capsule sponge vs no screening **$26,358–$33,307 per quality-adjusted life-year** (under the $50,000 threshold); **endoscopy vs capsule sponge $107,583–$330,361** (over it). ⚠ **But a cheap test does not automatically save money** — applied to a wider population its positives all funnel back into endoscopy, and the saving "could be reduced, eliminated, or even reversed." These tools **enrich** a defined high-risk population; they do not widen it.
- **The case-finding failure numbers are now on the page's existing pitfall box**, where they belong: **<10%** of esophageal-adenocarcinoma patients carry a prior Barrett's diagnosis, **~40%** never had GERD, **~50%** of short-segment disease is symptom-free, and only **~10%** of symptomatic GERD patients are scoped in a year.
- **[[capsule-endoscopy]] gains an `### Esophageal Capsule — not a recommended screening test` subsection** — pooled **77%/86%**, the specificity swing by reference standard (90% endoscopic vs 73% histologic), and the three disqualifiers: **no biopsy capability**, limited device control, and **esophageal capsule retention in 0.7%–2.2%**, usually from an **unsuspected stricture**. Also the distinction a reader will otherwise miss: the accepted nonendoscopic test is the capsule **sponge**, a different device.
- **Source priority applied, not flattened.** [[acg-2022-barretts]] governs the recommendation — capsule sponge plus biomarker is an acceptable alternative modality. The 2018 "we do not recommend any alternative test" is recorded as superseded history, which the document's own sub-recommendation 2a predicted.
- ⚠ **[[nejm-2023-fever-returning-traveler]] remains the one orphan**, unchanged. Out of budget this pass, and it is the same kind of job: real content to move onto entity pages, not a link to add.

CLAUDE.md → *Missing source pages* ranks by **tier** first (guidelines/CPUs/consensus/RCTs before other primary research), and Lewis 1997 is a tier-2 score-derivation paper while 20 of the 35 arrivals are tier-1 society guidelines or international consensus statements. Tier-1 therefore goes first this pass; Lewis 1997 and the other score papers keep their place at the head of the tier-2 queue.

**Ingested (file 1): [[acg-asge-2026-ercp-quality-indicators|ACG/ASGE 2026 Quality Indicators for ERCP]] — the companion the colonoscopy set was missing, and it closes a gap [[ercp]] had declared on itself.**

- Picked first: the newest tier-1 document in the batch (published online December 2025, *Am J Gastroenterol* 2026;121:80–95), and the second of the three documents in the `needed-sources.md` quality-indicator row the 2026-10-24 pass opened.
- **All 13 indicators captured** with the task force's own strength grade, measure type and target, plus the **5 priority indicators** (accepted indication, deep cannulation, stone extraction, rectal NSAID, unplanned hospital visit).
- **New page [[ercp-quality-indicators]]** owns the set — [[ercp]] is already ~2,950 body words, so copying the table there would have made a long page longer. It mirrors [[colonoscopy-quality-indicators]] exactly.
- **[[ercp]]'s own gap line is deleted, not re-flagged.** `## Quality Metrics` said in reader-facing text that the cannulation-rate, appropriate-indication and PEP-rate benchmarks "are set in the ASGE/ACG *Quality Indicators for ERCP* document, not in the sources cited on this page". It now points at the new page and keeps only the ASGE 2015 procedural-success benchmarks it owns.
- **The practice change: rectal indomethacin or diclofenac is now a 1A indicator in *unselected* patients** with an intact papilla, not high-risk only as in 2015 — measured at **>90%**, against current delivery to **well under half** of patients. The 90%-rather-than-98% target is deliberate, to allow for allergy, renal dysfunction and the very-low-risk.
- ⚠ **A silent denominator change, same failure family as the 2024 ADR denominator.** Stone extraction is no longer limited to stones **<1 cm** — the denominator is now **all extrahepatic duct stones** after successful cannulation. A provider's historical rate is not comparable to the >90% target, and nothing about the number announces which definition produced it. Flagged on the new page.
- ⚠ **Indicators 11–13 are *process* measures** — they score how often PEP, post-sphincterotomy hemorrhage and cholangitis are **documented and tracked**, not how often they occur. The document deliberately **sets no performance target for the PEP rate itself**, holding that a single fair benchmark is not feasible. Recorded explicitly so a later pass does not "fix" this into a rate target.
- **Grades are the task force's own 8-level scheme (1A/1B/1C+/1C/2A/2B/2C/3), not GRADE** — 6 of the 13 are graded **3 = expert opinion only**. Same vocabulary trap as the colonoscopy document; stated on both new pages.
- **Table 2 is not this document's content.** It reprints the 19 indicators common to all GI endoscopic procedures, which are issued and discussed in the Elmunzer companion article — also in this batch, ingested next. Those indicators are cited to the companion, not here.
- **Propagation (4 further pages):**
  - [[sphincter-of-oddi-dysfunction]] — EPISOD **held at 5 years**, manometry **neither reproducible nor predictive**, type III now a **disorder of gut–brain interaction**; plus the surviving carve-out (papillary stenosis with biliary-type pain **and** elevated liver enzymes or a dilated duct), with the warning that the duct also dilates with age, cholecystectomy and opioid use.
  - [[pancreas-divisum]] — the page said "ongoing sham-controlled RCT … is underway". **It reported, and it was negative:** a large multicentre sham-controlled RCT at DDW 2025 found minor papilla sphincterotomy **did not** significantly reduce recurrence. Abstract form only, and the page says so.
  - [[antibiotic-prophylaxis-endoscopy]] — the three supported ERCP scenarios (anticipated/actual incomplete drainage, **cholangioscopy**, post-liver-transplant), ASGE's shift of the post-transplant indication **from universal to conditional**, no data for pancreatoscopy, and that **withholding it where no benefit is likely is part of the same indicator**.
  - [[choledocholithiasis]] — measured performance of the two criteria sets: **2010 positive predictive value 62%** (high-risk category held a stone only 73.6% of the time) versus **2019 sensitivity 96.87%, PPV 89.57%**.
- **Cards — 8 new notes on `7-concepts/ercp-quality-indicators`.** Cannulation target and the anatomy it assumes; the two situations scored as a failed ERCP (rescue EUS-BD, duodenal obstruction); the cost of persisting at a difficult cannulation; the stone-extraction target and its widened denominator; the rectal-NSAID target and denominator; the three consensus PEP criteria; the two 30-day unplanned-event rates; the radiation measurement to record. **Nothing was carded that the deck already owns** — the rectal-NSAID regimen and contraindications, the prophylactic-pancreatic-stent indications, specification and follow-up radiograph are all already carded on `ercp` from [[asge-2023-post-ercp-pancreatitis]], so they were left there under the one-owner rule.

The card file is written, and the `.md` is the source of truth; the next host-side card pass will rebuild and report any cap violation. **Ingested (file 2): [[asge-acg-2024-common-endoscopy-quality-indicators|ASGE/ACG 2024 Quality Indicators Common to All GI Endoscopic Procedures]] — the base layer under the other two, and the row in `needed-sources.md` is now closed.**

- The third of the three documents named in the quality-indicator row (Rex 2024 landed on 2026-10-24, Anderson 2026 above). **Row deleted from `wiki/needed-sources.md`** — all three are in.

Stated on the source page so no later pass silently picks one.

  - [[endoscopy-sedation]] — the **full ASA fasting set** (clear liquids 2 h · milk 6 h · light meal 6 h · **fried or fatty meal 8 h**), which **resolves an apparent conflict the page had been carrying**: its ASGE "6 h light meal" and AGA "8 h solids" lines are describing different meals, not disagreeing. Plus the longer fast for gastroparesis/achalasia/obstruction, and that **the bowel preparation is not a fasting violation** — residual gastric fluid is **<25 mL** whether the prep was split or taken entirely the evening before.
  - [[anticoagulation-gi-bleeding]] — pitfall box: **81–325 mg daily aspirin is safe for almost every endoscopic procedure** and should **not** be interrupted when taken for secondary cardiovascular prevention; inappropriate cessation is frequent and educable, and **cold snare resection of small polyps on clopidogrel may not require cessation**.
  - [[colonoscopy-quality-indicators]], [[ercp-quality-indicators]] — cross-linked to the base layer.

Only the net-new material was moved onto those pages; the rest is a link.

No fact was carded on a non-owner page to raise the count.

**Ingested (file 3): [[sages-2024-hiatal-hernia-surgery|SAGES 2024 Guidelines for the Surgical Treatment of Hiatal Hernias]] — [[hiatal-hernia]] finally has a guideline about hiatal hernia.**

- Until this pass the page was built **entirely on GERD guidelines**, where hiatal hernia appears only as the anatomic variable that selects an antireflux procedure. It had **no type I–IV definitions** and nothing at all on paraesophageal hernia surgery.
- **All four key questions captured with the force the panel actually used**, which is the point of this document: **one conditional, low-certainty recommendation** (add a fundoplication during type II–IV repair), **one explicit decision not to make a recommendation** (mesh), and **two expert opinions** (repair of an asymptomatic hernia; conversion to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass for recurrence). **Certainty was low for every question.**
- ⚠ **The mesh item is a non-recommendation, not a recommendation against.** The panel *considered* conditionally recommending against routine mesh — benefits and harms looked balanced, "why add an extra step?" — and rejected it because the confidence intervals leave room for mesh being either beneficial or harmful. Flagged on the source page so a later pass does not upgrade it; this is the same failure family the memory file records for `asge-2020-endoscopic-removal`.
- **Effect sizes carried, not just directions.** Fundoplication: objective reflux relative risk **0.31** (321 fewer per 1000), recurrence **0.55**, leak **0.33**, against late dysphagia **2.94** (25 more per 1000). Mesh: only **late total dysphagia** reached significance (**0.49**, 108 fewer per 1000); **no mesh erosions** across 3 RCTs and 270 patients.
- **The most clinically useful content is in the expert-opinion sections**, and it is criteria rather than thresholds: how to establish a patient is genuinely asymptomatic (**dyspnea, exercise intolerance, abnormal echocardiogram** — non-GI symptoms secondary to the hernia), when watchful waiting is reasonable, and the six circumstances favouring RYGB over redo repair.
- ⚠ **Three gaps stated for the reader rather than filled:** no hernia-size threshold at which repair becomes indicated, no body mass index threshold for weight loss before repair, and **no way to predict who will develop gastric volvulus** (organo-axial rotation is the only feature named as concerning). The page says so; nothing was supplied from elsewhere.
- **Propagation:** [[hiatal-hernia]] gains the type table in `## Assessment` and a new `#### Paraesophageal (type II–IV) hernia — the surgical questions` subsection under Therapeutics, plus three new lines in its existing *What the guidelines deliberately do not say* section. Do not rely on mtime alone — the count-vs-baseline check is still what *detects* a delivery — but once a folder's count is over baseline, `ls -lt` on it is a fast way to name the arrivals. `git status` remains useless either way.*
